title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #3

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the main job of leaves? (1 mark)
   A. Making seeds
   B. Taking in water from the soil
   C. Holding the plant in the soil
   D. Making food for the plant

2. Maize lives for one season and then dies. A baobab lives for many years. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Only maize is alive
   B. Baobab does not die
   C. Plants live for different lengths of time
   D. Maize never grows

3. Why do farmers remove weeds from a crop field? (1 mark)
   A. To make weeds grow
   B. So crops get enough water, light and space
   C. To harm the crops
   D. To stop rain falling

4. What does the stem do? (1 mark)
   A. Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   B. Makes food using sunlight
   C. Makes seeds
   D. Only takes in water

5. Which of these is a safety rule when handling plants? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   B. Rub sap on your eyes
   C. Taste every fruit you find
   D. Pull plants with thorns barehanded

6. Which of these is a way that people benefit from plants? (1 mark)
   A. They make noise
   B. They give food, shade and wood
   C. They cause floods
   D. They give plastic

7. A tadpole grows into a frog. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Animals do not grow
   B. Only fish grow
   C. Animals grow and change
   D. Tadpoles are plants

8. Which of these is a crab? (1 mark)
   A. A bird
   B. An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   C. A mammal
   D. A vertebrate with fur

9. Which of these animals lays eggs? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Human
   D. Cow

10. Which of these statements is true? (1 mark)
   A. All animals can fly
   B. All fish have a backbone
   C. All small animals are insects
   D. All animals have six legs

11. Which of these animals is a reptile? (1 mark)
   A. Tilapia
   B. Lizard
   C. Butterfly
   D. Hen

12. Which of these is a mammal? (1 mark)
   A. Tilapia
   B. Cow
   C. Crocodile
   D. Frog

13. A pupil finds a small animal under a stone. It has a long soft body, no legs and no shell. It is probably (1 mark)
   A. A frog
   B. A snake
   C. An earthworm
   D. A lizard

14. What does the large intestine do with the leftovers? (1 mark)
   A. Swallows them
   B. Takes back water and forms faeces
   C. Turns them into saliva
   D. Chews them

15. Which of these is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Only tea
   B. Ugali, vegetables and beans
   C. Only soda
   D. Only sweets

16. In the mouth, which part helps to move food around and swallow? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Stomach
   C. Gullet
   D. Tongue

17. Which of these leaves the body through the anus? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach juice
   B. Blood
   C. Faeces
   D. Saliva

18. Sand pours like a liquid. What state is each grain? (1 mark)
   A. Steam
   B. Solid
   C. Liquid
   D. Gas

19. Which state of matter has its own shape and fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Steam only
   B. Solid
   C. Liquid
   D. Gas

20. Which of these can be made from waste for the classroom? (1 mark)
   A. A dustbin
   B. A new mountain
   C. A house
   D. A car engine

21. What is a compost pit used for? (1 mark)
   A. Storing plastic
   B. Storing glass
   C. Burning waste
   D. Turning kitchen waste into manure

22. What is a good use of old clothes? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them in a drain
   B. Use them as cleaning cloths
   C. Burn them near a house
   D. Bury them in a garden pit

23. Why is burning plastic bad? (1 mark)
   A. It makes good manure
   B. It makes rain
   C. It is safe for everyone
   D. It makes harmful smoke

24. Which of these is a reason to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. There will be enough for everyone
   B. To make it more expensive
   C. To make taps rust
   D. To waste less time

25. Which of these is an example of reducing water wastage? (1 mark)
   A. Washing with lots of water
   B. Ignoring leaks
   C. Leaving the hose on
   D. Closing a tap after use

26. Who should practise water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Everyone at home and school
   C. Only adults
   D. Only farmers

27. Why are tyres made with rough patterns? (1 mark)
   A. To make them lighter
   B. To make them shiny
   C. To grip the road
   D. To reduce friction

28. Which of these is NOT an effect of force? (1 mark)
   A. Changing shape
   B. Stopping motion
   C. Starting motion
   D. Making something have colour

29. A flat sheet of paper falls slower than a stone because (1 mark)
   A. Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   B. Paper is bigger
   C. Gravity does not pull paper
   D. The stone is bigger

30. Which force slows down or stops a book sliding on the floor? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Gravity
   C. Heat
   D. Friction

31. What happens if there is no friction between your shoes and the ground? (1 mark)
   A. You stop
   B. You walk faster
   C. You slip
   D. You fly

32. Pulling a rope in tug of war uses (1 mark)
   A. Only heat
   B. Only light
   C. Only gravity
   D. A pull force

33. Which of these reduces friction? (1 mark)
   A. Rough paint
   B. Ball bearings
   C. Sand on a surface
   D. Gluing parts

34. Which of these is a safe practice with light? (1 mark)
   A. Stare at bright lights
   B. Look at the sun with your eyes
   C. Never look straight at the sun
   D. Shine torches in eyes

35. Which of these only reflects light? (1 mark)
   A. A firefly
   B. A candle
   C. A torch
   D. The moon

36. What do solar panels change sunlight into? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Electricity
   C. Sound
   D. Water

37. Which of these is translucent? (1 mark)
   A. Wood
   B. Stone
   C. Clear glass
   D. Tissue paper

38. Why do we boil water before drinking if it may be unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Heat makes water heavy
   B. Heat removes all salt
   C. Heat makes water sweet
   D. Heat kills germs

39. Why are pot handles often made of wood or plastic? (1 mark)
   A. They pass heat quickly
   B. They are heavy
   C. They pass heat slowly
   D. They get very hot

40. Where should children be when an adult is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. On top of the cooker
   B. Holding the pot
   C. Away from the fire
   D. Next to the fire

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why the flat paper and stone dropped together do not land at the same time. (3 marks)

42. Name the part of a plant that makes food and the part that makes seeds. (2 marks)

43. Name the three main sources of heat. (2 marks)

44. Explain the difference between reusing and recycling. (3 marks)

45. A pupil pulls up a small bean plant from the garden. Describe what she will see and give the job of each part she sees. (5 marks)

46. Describe how a poster can teach the community about water conservation. Give four features. (4 marks)

47. Describe how you would show that light travels in a straight line. (3 marks)

48. Explain how a frog is similar to and different from a fish. (4 marks)

49. Explain why plastic bags are a danger to the environment. (3 marks)

50. Explain the dangers of diarrhoea and what should be done to help someone who has it. (5 marks)

51. Describe how waste attracts pests that harm health. (3 marks)

52. Describe three examples each of reducing and reusing water. (4 marks)

53. Explain how animals show the signs of life: feeding, growing, and reproducing. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

54. What should you do for a small burn? State three actions. (3 marks)

55. Describe how kitchen waste can be turned into manure. (3 marks)

56. Describe five ways in which forces are used at home and on the farm. (5 marks)

57. Explain how ball bearings help a bicycle move. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Making food for the plant
   Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food.

2. C — Plants live for different lengths of time
   All plants die, but some live for one season and others for many years.

3. B — So crops get enough water, light and space
   Weeds compete with crops for water, light and room.

4. A — Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   The stem supports the plant and carries water and food.

5. A — Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   Some plants can hurt or poison people, so ask first.

6. B — They give food, shade and wood
   Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood and clean air.

7. C — Animals grow and change
   Young animals grow and may change shape as they become adults.

8. B — An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   A crab has no backbone and has a hard shell outside.

9. A — Hen
   A hen lays eggs. The others give birth to live young.

10. B — All fish have a backbone
   Fish are vertebrates. Small animals may be spiders, worms or others.

11. B — Lizard
   A lizard has dry scaly skin.

12. B — Cow
   A cow has hair and feeds its calf on milk.

13. C — An earthworm
   An earthworm is a soft, legless invertebrate.

14. B — Takes back water and forms faeces
   Water is absorbed and the rest becomes solid waste.

15. B — Ugali, vegetables and beans
   A balanced meal has energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.

16. D — Tongue
   The tongue moves food and helps swallowing.

17. C — Faeces
   Faeces leave the body through the anus.

18. B — Solid
   Each grain is a small solid.

19. B — Solid
   Solids keep their shape and volume.

20. A — A dustbin
   A dustbin can be made from waste materials like a bucket or box.

21. D — Turning kitchen waste into manure
   Decomposable waste rots into compost.

22. B — Use them as cleaning cloths
   Reusing old cloth as cleaning cloths reduces waste.

23. D — It makes harmful smoke
   Burning plastic gives off harmful smoke.

24. A — There will be enough for everyone
   Conserving leaves water for others.

25. D — Closing a tap after use
   Closing taps stops the flow of water.

26. B — Everyone at home and school
   Everyone shares water and should save it.

27. C — To grip the road
   Grip needs friction.

28. D — Making something have colour
   Colour is not caused by a force.

29. A — Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   Air pushes up more on the wide flat sheet.

30. D — Friction
   Friction opposes the movement between surfaces.

31. C — You slip
   Without friction you cannot grip.

32. D — A pull force
   Pulling is a force.

33. B — Ball bearings
   Ball bearings roll and reduce friction.

34. C — Never look straight at the sun
   Looking at the sun harms eyes.

35. D — The moon
   The moon reflects sunlight.

36. B — Electricity
   Solar panels make electricity from sunlight.

37. D — Tissue paper
   Tissue paper lets some light through.

38. D — Heat kills germs
   Boiling kills many germs.

39. C — They pass heat slowly
   Handles stay cooler.

40. C — Away from the fire
   Children stay away from the cooker.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity pulls both down but air pushes up on the flat paper more, so it falls slowly. The stone is little affected by the air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for gravity on both, 1 mark for air pushing paper, 1 mark for stone landing first.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaves make food and flowers (fruits) make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun, fire and electricity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reusing means using an item again in the same or a new way without changing it, for example a bottle for water. Recycling means turning waste into a new product, for example melting old plastic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reuse, 1 mark for recycle, 1 mark for one example.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: She will see roots that hold the plant and take in water, a stem that holds it up and carries food and water, leaves that make food, and maybe flowers or pods that make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming each of four parts and 1 mark for correct function overall.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: A clear message, big pictures, short slogan, bright colours, ideas for saving water, placed where many people see it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four features.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use three cards with holes in the middle and line them up in a row. Shine a torch through the holes. Light passes. Move the middle card and the light is blocked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both are vertebrates and have a backbone. A frog has moist skin and lives on land and in water, and a fish lives in water and has gills and fins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for similarity and 2 marks for differences.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: They stay for many years, block drains, harm animals that eat them and pollute land and water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: The body loses water quickly and the person becomes weak, especially young children. They should drink clean water and ORS, rest, see a health worker and keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 3 marks for actions.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rotting waste attracts flies, rats and cockroaches. They spread germs to food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea and cholera.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pests, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for diseases.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: close taps, fix leaks, use a cup. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants, laundry water for mopping, rainwater for the garden.
   Working / marking points: Award marks for correct examples up to a total of 4.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Feeding: a goat eats grass. Growing: a chick becomes a hen. Reproducing: a hen lays eggs, or a cow gives birth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with example, plus 1 mark for explaining growth as getting bigger.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water, cover with a clean cloth, tell an adult and do not put butter or oil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put peelings and other kitchen waste with dry leaves and some soil in a compost pit. Decomposers rot it and after some weeks it turns to compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the pit, 1 mark for decomposers, 1 mark for compost.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Pushing a wheelbarrow, pulling a plough, lifting water from a well with a rope, hammering a nail, kicking a ball, stitching clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are small steel balls in the wheel. They roll between moving parts, so there is less friction and the wheels turn easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what they are, 1 mark for rolling, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for wheels turning easily.
